title: Puré de Papas con Despojos (Potato Purée with Meat Scraps)
description: Prepared with meat, onions, and carrots.
steps: Place in a pot six onions and six medium carrots made into slices, and on top throw the scraps of meat and poultry with a glass of water or broth.
Place over high heat.
When all has taken on a nice color, dampen with boiling water, adding a bouquet garnished with cloves and a little salt.
Leave to cook for an hour and a half over moderate heat, pressing and compressing the meats during cooking so they release their juice.
Pass through a sieve and when cold pour slowly into the pot or serving dish.
The meats are put in the pot and communicate good flavor to it.

title: Quenelles Communes (Common Quenelles)
description: Prepared with fish or beef, bread, and butter.

ingredients.name: at least half a pound of domestic poultry, fish, or beef
ingredients.sourceText: at least half a pound of domestic poultry, fish, or beef

steps: Finely mince at least half a pound of any of these meats
Pass through a quenelles sieve
Add prepared bread crumbs
Grind everything together on a metate with butter, salt and pepper
Beat two or three egg yolks and incorporate them
Beat egg whites with a wooden spoon and fold in
Heat broth or water with butter and salt until boiling
Fill a spoon with the prepared filling, smoothing it with a knife dipped in hot water
Place the spoon over lukewarm water and empty it onto white paper
When the paper is full, bring the broth to a boil and gently place the paper with the quenelles in it
Remove quenelles as they detach themselves
Move the pot to the edge of the stove and cook for ten minutes
Remove the quenelles from the broth

title: Quenelles de Gazapo o de Conejo (Rabbit or Hare Quenelles)
description: Prepared with rabbit or hare, bread, and broth.
steps: Lift the slices from the rabbits and take the legs, separating the meat from the sinews with the tip of the knife
Pound the meat well and pass it through a quenelles sieve and gather it into a pile
Soak bread crumb in milk, broth and hot water, and when well soaked place it in a clean new cloth and squeeze as much as possible so no liquid remains
Pound it perfectly afterward and pass it through the same quenelles sieve as the meat, making another pile separate
If the butter is very hard, pound it also, making a third pile, ensuring the three portions are equal in quantity of bread, meat, and butter
Mix the three piles together and pound them jointly, then add salt, coarse pepper, a little grated nutmeg and one spoonful of salsa rizada
Pound the mixture again, adding from time to time an egg yolk until three are complete, then add two whole eggs

When the mass is at the right consistency, make a small ball and throw it into a pot or kettle with boiling water to test if it is too firm, in which case add a small piece of butter to the mass; but if it is too soft or delicate, add an egg yolk

If you want quenelles with more body and better quality, put beef udder in place of butter, cooking it in the pot and passing it through the quenelles sieve after frying; put more quantity of udder in the mass than the amount of butter that would have been used
After everything is mixed, conclude the operation as with common quenelles

title: Queso de Cabeza de Puerco (Pork Head Cheese with Spices)
description: Prepared with pork, tongue, and vinegar.
steps: Cut the head into large pieces removing a piece of jowl if it were very large
Cook everything with the tongue with salt and aromatic herbs
When cooked but not too much so it does not fall apart, set aside, remove the bones and cut into small pieces
Do the same with the tongue
Grind well twenty-five cloves and thirty thin peppercorns, a regular piece and a small ground nutmeg
Mix from the metate with one cup of Castilian vinegar and another of wine of Jerez
Mix everything with the head already cut, and place in a pan, adding more salt if needed, ground

Parboil everything well and while hot place in a cloth bag a quarter in circumference so it comes out large, tie as tightly as possible and place to press with considerable weight on top so the fat comes out, making sure it comes out well rounded and the tied part remains in the middle
When cold, unsew the bag to remove it
If desired the feet can be added, only add more spices, wine and vinegar in proportion to the amount

title: Queso de Cerdo a la Española (Spanish-Style Pork Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with pig's head, garlic, and vinegar.
steps: Clean the pig's head well, debone it, and remove all the meat and fat without damaging the skin.
Cut the meat into very thin strips; do the same with the fat, placing each in separate dishes.

Cut the ears also into very thin strips, and season everything on top and bottom with salt, black pepper, allspice, thyme, laurel, basil, six cloves of spice, a little culantro, and half nutmeg, all ground or chopped very fine, adding two garlic cloves and one whole bunch of parsley.

Place the pig's head skin in a round pot and arrange in it all the seasoned meat strips, with a little vinegar, some small pieces of ham if available, and some parsley leaves, which are arranged very neatly, continuing the same way to the end.
Sew up the skin leaving it like a bag; wrap it in clean linen, tie it very well with twine or hemp cord.

Put this cheese in a pot or marmite that fits its size well, and cook for about six or seven hours with broth, two cuartillos of white wine, onion, carrot, thyme, laurel, basil, one garlic clove, salt, and pepper.
When cooked, place it to drain and put it in a round vessel that serves as a mold, cover it with a lid and a large weight on top so it takes the shape of a cheese, leaving it thus until it is cold.

title: Queso de Cerdo a la Italiana (Italian-Style Pork Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with liver, fat, and pepper.
steps: Mash a pig's liver with two-thirds of its weight of fat and one-third of jowl; mix well and season with pepper, salt, spices, thyme, sage, laurel, basil, chopped parsley, culantro and crushed anise, and scraped nutmeg.
Cover the sides and bottom of a tin mold with caul fat; place the chopped mixture on top and cover everything with slices of fat, putting it to cook in the oven.
When cooked, let it cool in the mold and remove it by soaking it in boiling water.

title: Quina (Quinine Liqueur)
description: Prepared with brandy, orange, and syrup.
steps: After grinding superior quinine into fine powder, place it to infuse in refined brandy and separating a little tincture to later give color to the liquor, distill in a bain-marie

Mix to the product two drops of orange essence for each quarter quart and after a day of resting, sweeten with clarified simple syrup, more or less concentrated in sugar, according to the desired sweetness and oiliness of the liquor; the common measure is to use one quarter quart of simple syrup for each quarter quart of recovered brandy
Then decant into stoppered large bottles and bottle immediately for use

title: Rabioles (Pasta Dumplings)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, meat, and flour.
steps: Mix 6 three egg yolks and a little broken pepper, combining well all these substances until a mass is formed that will be seasoned with fine salt
To a pound of flour add three fresh eggs, and stir until forming a mass that is seasoned with fine salt
With a rolling pin form from it a sheet as thin as paper, dusting it with a little dry flour
Place short pieces of the prepared filling on half of the sheet at equal distance from each other
Moisten the other half of the flour sheet by sprinkling it with wine, and cover it pressing so it adheres at the edges of the filling

Cut equal and small squares, which will be placed for a little time over not very strong fire until they cook, which will be known when they float, then separate from the fire and place them drained of broth in another vessel
Take the soup tureen, and pouring in a little of the stew broth, place a layer of rabioles
On top add sufficient grated Flanders or La Barca cheese
Then a little melted butter, pouring on top more stew, which should be boiling
Thus multiply the layers of rabioles, cheese, butter and stew until filling the platter that will be served

title: Rabioles con Carne de Puerco y Requesón (Pasta Parcels with Pork and Fresh Cheese)
description: Prepared with pork, cheese, and beef marrow.
steps: Chop raw pork loin and grind with beef marrow, fresh cheese curds, and half-cooked spinach
Remove all skin and tendons from the meat and mix with three or four raw eggs, good grated cheese, sufficient salt and pepper, and a little good cooking oil
Once well mixed and the filling paste formed, moisten sufficient flour with warm water
Mix two or three eggs into the dough according to quantity and add a little salt
Mix everything well so the dough is soft and divide into three or four portions
Cover with a damp cloth and dust the work surface with dry flour
Extend each portion one by one with a rolling pin until it forms a sheet as thin as paper
Place balls of filling at equal distances on the sheet of dough
Fold part of the dough to cover them and press the edges of the covered dough balls with three fingers
Cut with a pastry wheel into small pastries or squares to form the rabioles
Bring salted water to boil in a pot and when boiling strongly, add the pastries in portions
Once they float, showing they are cooked, remove with a skimmer and drain without letting them stick
Cut veal or beef pulp into regular pieces and fry with lard in a pot until browned
Add a pair of garlic heads and whole onions, ground pepper and sufficient salt
Moisten with a quarter of Jerez wine and a few bay leaves
When the pot comes to a boil, increase the broth by adding water or meat broth
Cover with an adjusted pot and seal the edges with paste, putting on low heat until the broth is well seasoned
Shake the pot occasionally so it does not burn
In a platter, make a layer of the pastries, cover well with another layer of grated cheese
Bathe with some of the stewed broth and continue multiplying layers of rabioles and cheese
Moisten with the stewed broth and place the soup over the steam of a pot until ready to serve

title: Rabioles con Nabos y Jamón (Rabioles with Turnips and Ham)
description: Prepared with turnips, ham, and lard.
steps: Make the dough with a pound of flour, 3 ounces of butter, 1 ounce of lard, 2 eggs, salt and necessary water

For the sauce, fry a little minced onion in butter and add water, salt, saffron for color, clove and pepper, all ground
Brown flour in butter letting it boil until well seasoned
Follow the same procedures of the previous articles for forming and cooking

title: Rabioles con Sesos (Pasta Parcels with Brains)
description: Prepared with brains, spinach, and fat.
steps: Cook a portion of spinach with a little tequesquite water
Form a filling by mixing the spinach with some fat ham, beef marrow, and brains, all cooked separately, adding fine salt
Add ground black pepper, cloves, and cinnamon to the filling, along with grated Flemish cheese, mixing well
Make a dough with flour, two or three eggs, and fine salt
Extend the dough on a table greased with melted lard until it forms very thin sheets
Place small pieces of spinach filling on the sheets at intervals
Cover with another sheet of dough and cut around the edges with a wheel or knife to form small pastries
Dust with flour so they do not stick and store for another day
The next day, cook the pastries gently in water with lard and fine salt so they do not fall apart
When cooked, drain well and place in the following broth
In a pot, add beef broth and toasted bread that has been ground well
Boil with necessary salt and when seasoned, add ground cinnamon, cloves, and enough pepper to stand out
Add a quarter of fresh butter and when it comes to a good boil, add the pastries
Keep on low heat until the broth thickens slightly
Remove from heat and serve with chopped parsley on top

description: Prepared with tomato, chile, and brains.

ingredients.name: half a wide chile toasted and deveined
ingredients.sourceText: half a wide chile toasted and deveined

steps: Mix a pound of flour with two egg yolks and one egg white, melted lard and salted water, and knead well until it forms small bubbles
For the filling, mix tomato, onion and deveined green chile all chopped very fine
Fry it with cooked chard and cooked brains also, adding 2 ground peppercorns and 2 ground cloves, a little oil and a little vinegar
Form and cook the rabioles following the same procedures of the previous articles
For the sauce, roast some tomatoes and squeeze them to remove all the seeds
Peel and grind them together with half a wide chile, toasted and deveined
Fry the ground mixture, adding a little ground sugar, 2 fine peppercorns and 2 cloves, water or pot broth, a little oil, vinegar and a little butter

title: Rabioles de Pechuga con Borraja y Requesón (Pasta Parcels with Chicken Breast, Borage, and Fresh Cheese)
description: Prepared with chicken breast, cheese, and borage.

ingredients.sourceText: beef leg larded with fat ham

ingredients.sourceText: Flemish or de la Barca cheese

ingredients.name: fresh cheese curds or very thick cooked milk
ingredients.sourceText: fresh cheese curds or very thick cooked milk

steps: Make a stew of beef leg larded with fat ham, garlic cloves, and cloves
Place in a pot with six large onions, six dried pasilla chiles, grated nutmeg, a bottle of Madeira or Jerez wine, and sufficient meat broth seasoned with fine salt
Boil over high heat until it thickens well; then place over two very low heats until it darkens without burning
Add more broth and give it a couple of boils, then remove from heat
When cooled, strain through a cloth to degrease it

Form a filling with chopped chicken breasts, grated Flemish or de la Barca cheese, bundles of cooked and chopped borage, fresh cheese curds or very thick cooked milk, grated nutmeg, ground cinnamon, two or three egg yolks, and a little broken pepper
Mix all these substances well until a paste forms and season with fine salt
To a pound of flour add three fresh eggs and mix until forming a dough seasoned with fine salt
Form with a rolling pin a sheet as thin as paper, dusting with some dry flour
Place portions of the prepared filling on half the sheet at equal distance
Moisten the other half of the flour sheet by sprinkling it

title: Rabioles Fritos (Fried Rabioles)
description: Prepared with lard, grated cheese, and butter or lard.

ingredients.name: beef marrow cooked in the same broth
ingredients.sourceText: beef marrow cooked in the same broth

steps: Make the dough with 14 ounces of flour, one egg, one spoonful of cold melted lard and the water needed for the flour to absorb
For the filling, make it with cooked chard chopped only in the green part, squeezed and seasoned with salt and ground pepper and mixed with grated cheese
Form the rabioles the same as in the preceding articles
Leave them on a board or tray to air until the next day
Fry them in butter or lard so they are not very golden, and cook them in seasoned chicken or pot broth

After cooking, separate them, and in the tureen or platter where they will be served, place a layer of grated cheese with ground pepper on top and another layer of rabioles, pouring a little of the same broth in which they were cooked
Continue placing layers until filling the tureen
On top of the last layer, in addition to cheese and pepper, place some small pieces of beef marrow that will have been cooked in the same rabioles broth, and other small pieces of butter
Place the platter over the steam of a pot or the tureen over hot coals so they stay hot without boiling and without the broth being consumed while they are carried to the table
Add some parsley leaves before serving

Dry them, pierce them with a sufficiently thick pin

Leave them in infusion for two months in twenty-four cuartillos of good aguardiente, which is aromatized with half a dram of nutmeg and another half dram of clove
After straining all the aguardiente laden with bitter and aromatic substance through a cloth or sieve without pressing the pomace, dissolve the necessary sugar to sweeten it
Leave the infusion to continue for another two months

ingredients.sourceText: half an ounce of brewer's yeast

Boil two quarts of cream and when boiling pour it over the yolks, stirring vigorously
Make it reach the proper point over the fire without letting it boil and pass through a cloth or sieve, letting it cool
Make yeast with {{source-5}}, half an ounce of brewer's foam and a little warm water, moistening it so it is somewhat soft
Let it ferment in a warm place
Soak another {{source-8}} with the cream mixture beaten with the yolks, adding {{source-9}}
Fold or gather the dough four or five times, add the yeast and fold two more times
Wrap the dough in a floured cloth, tie it firmly and let it rise or ferment in a warm place, taking about four hours to be in good condition
Then cut the pieces or little gifts the size of an egg, shaping them as desired by molding
Let them air or ferment more, about half an hour on a sheet
After browning put them in the oven
When cooked, open them on one side, remove a little of the crumb and put in their place butter kneaded with salt
Serve

title: Regalitos de Masa de Queso (Small Cheese Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with cheese, water or milk, and butter.

ingredients.name: cheese, buttered, lightly salted, and 10-12 days old
ingredients.sourceText: 1.5 pounds cheese, buttered, lightly salted, and 10-12 days old

steps: Knead 1.5 pounds of buttered, salted cheese that is 10-12 days old on a table with your hands until it becomes a lump-free mass
Add 1.5 pounds of fresh good butter, salt, and 8 or 9 eggs
Spread this mixture on a table and add 1 glass of water or milk
When moistened and as liquid as beaten egg, incorporate first 3 pounds 12 ounces of flour and then another 2 pounds 4 ounces, setting aside 2 handfuls of this flour for later
When the dough is well bound, dust with some of the reserved flour and knead 2 or 3 times, but gently, over the course of half an hour
Then spread and let rest in this state for no more than a quarter hour
Roll lengthwise and cut the small pastries to the desired size and thickness of two fingers
Place on paper greased with fresh butter
Arrange them, lift the edges, and bake in the oven
With the oven well covered, half an hour is sufficient for them to cook
Watch from time to time to ensure they do not burn

title: Relleno Cocido de Ave (Cooked Poultry Stuffing)
description: Prepared with chicken, bread, and broth.
steps: Cut chicken breasts into dice and place in a casserole with a little butter, salt, black pepper and nutmeg
Simmer gently over very low heat for ten minutes
Remove the breasts, drain them and let them cool
In the same casserole, add a piece of bread crumb with broth and a little finely chopped parsley
Stir everything with a wooden spoon, pressing and reducing it to a paste
When the broth is consumed and the bread is well cooked, set aside and let cool
Prepare a cooked and cold cow udder, or use butter as a substitute
Pound the poultry breasts and when well ground, pass them through a quenelle sieve and set aside
Similarly pound the bread crumb and pass through the sieve, setting also apart
Pound the udder, pass through the sieve and keep separate
Make three equal portions of breast, bread and udder, and pound them together in the mortar
After grinding for three quarters of an hour, add five or six egg yolks according to the quantity of stuffing
Pound the yolks together with everything else as they are added
This stuffing can be used equally in crusts with all kinds of dishes

title: Relleno para un Pastel (Filling for a Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with chicken, stock, and macaroni or noodles.
steps: Prepare in advance: have 1 chicken well cooked with seasonings, deboned and cut into small pieces
Have 4 or 5 dozen meatballs (the size of a one-ounce bullet) prepared and cooked as usual
Have ready a good stew or braised stock that should be thick, colored and substantial
Boil macaroni or thick noodles in salted water until not too soft
Drain through a colander
In the prepared cooking pot, layer the ingredients: a few noodles with grated Flanders cheese, some meatballs, some cooked chicken, a pinch of cinnamon, and some of the stew stock
Continue layering until the pot is filled
Cover with the dough layer and seal it at the edges so the pastry is well closed
Brush the top surface with a feather using beaten egg yolk
Sprinkle sugar on top
Put in a very hot oven; when almost done (which can be seen from the covering dough), cool slightly and turn onto a round platter to serve

title: Requesón Inglés (English Curd Cheese)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, lemon, and white wine.
steps: Mix six egg yolks with six quartillos of milk
Sweeten it and place on the fire
When it is boiling, squeeze a lemon into it
As soon as the milk curdles, remove from heat
Pour into a cloth that is tied, letting all the whey strain out
Reserve the requesón in the same cloth until the next day
Untie the cloth and slice the requesón
Pour nine strained egg yolks into the whey
Place on the fire and let it thicken
Arrange the slices of requesón on a plate
Pour the thickened whey on top
Add a little white wine

title: Requesón y Almendra (Dulce de) (Sweet of Ricotta and Almond)
description: Prepared with almond, cheese, and egg yolks.
steps: Make the ricotta paste with the difference of using only one pound of ricotta, and adding four ounces of cooked egg yolks and one ounce of pine nuts, all ground separately
Make another almond paste that should be somewhat loose, regulating for each pound of almond two pounds of clarified syrup at the point of gathering in water

Put in a platter a layer of biscuit soaked in milk cooked with sugar and cinnamon, and slightly squeezed with the hands, another of ricotta paste, another of biscuit, another of almond paste, another of egg yolk paste, another of pine nuts and in this manner until the plate is filled, the last layer being ricotta, and concluding everything as stated in the preceding article

Add a little chopped parsley, empty the pan, and serve the kidneys

description: Prepared with mutton, melted butter, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Prepare twelve mutton kidneys by wetting them and opening them slightly on the side opposite the nerve
Remove the skins covering them and finish opening them without separating the parts
Thread them through, four at a time, on a wooden skewer or in its place a thick popote, so they cannot join or group together
Dip them in melted butter, cover with breadcrumbs, and place on the grill, taking care to turn them appropriately
When cooked, remove them from the skewers and arrange on a plate
Place on each one about half a walnut of cold mayordomo sauce
Heat the plate and squeeze lemon juice over it

title: Rol Pincé (Dutch Beef Roll)
description: A bread preparation made with beef, salt, and pepper.

ingredients.name: beef, preferably from the ribs
ingredients.sourceText: six pounds of beef, preferably from the ribs

steps: Take six pounds of beef, being better from the covered ribs, cut into pieces and mince everything together as for pastry filling, and season with salt, pepper, spices and nutmeg.

Prepare in advance a very clean beef tripe which is cut into square pieces of eight inches, more or less, and fill on the interior part with the minced meat; join the extremities of the wrapped pieces and sew them with a large needle.

Boil water with a good handful of salt and a quarter of vinegar in a very well-tinned pot, or better in a large pot where all the rolls fit comfortably, which are thrown into the boiling water and left to boil for the space of one hour; they are then drained on a clean cloth, and put in a jar of sandstone or in an unglazed pot, with the necessary vinegar to cover them; do not cover the jar until everything is perfectly cold, and these rolls can be used after fifteen days if you do not employ them all in that time, then leave the remaining ones in the vinegar only after that time.

description: Prepared with turbot, salt, and water.
steps: After preparing the turbot as indicated in the first article, place about {{source-1}} at the bottom of a kettle and fill it with water, giving it two or three boils

title: Rombo en Caldillo Ligero (Turbot in Light Broth)
description: A soup made with turbot, lemon juice, and butter or sauce or cream.

ingredients.name: Three or four quartillos of milk
ingredients.sourceText: Three or four quartillos of milk

steps: Select the largest turbot, which should be thick and of very white flesh
Remove the roe and entrails by making an opening near the head
Wash many times, changing the water
Remove two or three vertebrae from the spine by opening it slightly on the dark side, and tie the jaw to the bone of the opening
Rub the entire surface with lemon juice
Place to cook in salt water, to which three or four quartillos of milk can be added
Apply strong heat at the stove, and when it begins to boil, reduce the heat so it finishes cooking without boiling
Keep hot and ten minutes before serving, drain it
Serve in fish platters on napkins adorned with fresh parsley and accompanied by a sauce boat with butter sauce or cream sauce

For the cream sauce: place four ounces of butter in a pan, one tablespoon of flour, salt, coarse pepper and half a quartillo of good milk; stir this sauce over the fire, and if it is too thick, add milk until it reaches the right consistency
Divide the cooked turbot into pieces, place in a pan and pour the sauce over it
Fry all of it making it jump, and keep it hot until serving time

title: Rombo en Marinesca (Turbot in Marinière Style)
description: Prepared with turbot, sauce, and onions.
steps: Choose a small turbot, empty it, wash it, let it drain, open it along the back, separate the flesh from the spine, and place a good raw Mayordomo sauce between the spine and the flesh
Chop two large onions and place them on a silver plate the size of the small turbot, with a piece of butter
Season with salt, coarse pepper, thyme, bay leaf in powder, chopped parsley and a little grated nutmeg
Arrange the small turbot over the onions, dust with salt, add lemon and melted butter, and moisten with half a bottle of white wine
Place the plate on a small burner and cover with a dome oven, letting it cook over very gentle heat
While it cooks, baste it frequently

steps: Place two or three pounds of sliced beef larded with ham in a pan with salt and pepper, a small bundle of parsley, fine herbs, onions studded with cloves, and two bay leaves
Sweat them over the fire, and when everything is stuck, add fresh butter with a little flour
Having made this red base thus, moisten with broth and scrape the bottom with the spoon
Wrap the turbot in ham slices and place to cook with a bottle of Champagne or other wine and with the beef base, placing the same beef on top
When the turbot is cooked, let it season over the embers, then dress it in the fish platter and serve with crab stew on top, bound with the substance of the crabs themselves

title: Rosquetes de Queso (Cheese Rings)
description: Prepared with cheese, egg yolks, and flour.

ingredients.name: Seven egg yolks per pound of cheese
ingredients.sourceText: Seven egg yolks per pound of cheese

steps: Choose fresh cheese that does not form strings when cooked
Crumble it and soak in water to remove salt
Strain through a sieve and let drain until dry
Grind the cheese
Mix seven egg yolks with each pound of cheese and a little flour so the dough is not too hard
To test consistency, coat the palm of the hand with butter, take a bit of dough and make a hole in the middle with your finger
Fry it; if it does not spread, rise, or burst, it has good consistency; otherwise add more flour until it is right
Form rosquetes like the test piece, or extrude them through a piping bag and fry
Boil them in clarified syrup made from two pounds of sugar, boiled with cinnamon and brought to medium consistency
When the rosquetes are well soaked in the syrup and dry, arrange on plates and decorate with pearl sugar, cinnamon powder, and anise seeds
They can also be left covered with syrup after boiling it more, in which case decorate only with cinnamon

steps: Beat thirty-two egg yolks with four ounces of very finely ground sugar and one piece of yeast the size of an egg, dissolved in a little lukewarm water
After the yolks are well beaten with the sugar and yeast, add a pinch of salt, one small cup of white wine and four ounces of very hot lard, being careful to mix all this well
Add flour until absorbed, so the dough is neither loose nor hard
Extend the dough with a rolling pin, making sure the sheet is neither very thin nor thick
Cut strips two fingers wide, and cut them to the desired size for the rosquetes
Seal the points together and form the little rings
Fry them in lard or butter until golden
Remove them and roll them in sugar and cinnamon

title: Rosquillas de Almendra (Almond Rings)
description: Prepared with almonds, egg whites, and water.
steps: Soak the almonds in hot water so that they can be peeled well
After peeling, place them in cold water, washing them several times
Dry them well in a cloth and grind them, lowering them from the metate with beaten egg whites to prevent them from forming oil
Once ground, have ready well-clarified syrup that is at the sheet point
For each pound of sugar that has been clarified, add one pound of ground almond, mix very well
When well incorporated, place on the fire, stirring constantly so it does not stick
When shaking the spoon quickly the dough does not stick, it is ready; remove from fire and empty it onto a plate sprinkled with sifted sugar until it has cooled well

Form pieces from it and put them in a tube or syringe that has a hole at the bottom in the shape of a star, or as desired, so that when the dough is pressed it comes out and the rosquillas are cut to the desired size by joining the two points together

After the rosquillas are formed, place them on papers that will be put in the oven at gentle heat, making sure they do not brown too much, and remove them from the oven as soon as they come off the paper
If you want to give them another flavor, you can add to the almond dough, before mixing it with the flour, juice or peel of orange, lemon or citron

title: Rosquillas de Almendra de Jeringa (Almond Syringe Rings)
description: Prepared with almonds, egg whites, and sugar.
steps: Soak the almonds, peel them, open them and dry them in the sun
The next day grind them well on a metate, rolling them with egg whites at medium beat
Then grind sugar and add two egg whites without beating, and mix this with the almonds while kneading it
Do this until the paste is in condition to come out of the syringe
Divide the product lengthwise and form the rings
Place them on paper, dust them with sugar and put them in the oven where they will remain until golden

title: Saladillo de Pecho de Puerco (Salted Pork Breast)
description: Prepared with pork, saltpeter, and salt.
steps: Divide the pork breast into medium-sized pieces and rub them with fine salt
Add a little saltpeter and pile the pieces one on top of another in a jar or pot, taking care to press them well to prevent air between them from giving them a rancid taste
To prevent this inconvenience, fill the gaps with salt, cover the vessel with a double clean cloth, and seal it as hermetically as possible
After eight or ten days the salted pork can be eaten, well dried, with the substance of chickpeas, peas, or lentils, or with turnips, or well with some stew of cabbages or other legumes

title: Salchichones de Bolonia (Bologna Sausages)
description: Prepared with meat, pork, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: Fresh, sound fat lard cut into large cubes
ingredients.sourceText: Fresh, sound fat lard cut into large cubes

steps: Separate the lean part from two hams and combine with two pork shoulders
Scrape with a knife and carefully remove all sinews
Mix the prepared meat with salt, whole pepper, cilantro, cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg, and bay leaf
Choose fresh, sound fat lard and cut into large cubes
Mix everything together and fill beef intestines, tying at both ends
Place in a vessel with saltpeter, cover well, and leave for eight days
Remove, drain, and tie between two sticks like a bundle of tobacco
Dry and smoke
When dry, untie, rub with a mixture of oil and wood ash, and hang in a suitable place to serve when desired

description: Prepared with pork, beef, and ham.

ingredients.name: Beef leg meat equal in weight
ingredients.sourceText: Beef leg meat equal in weight

steps: Chop the lean pork meat and mix with beef leg meat equal in weight
Cut ham into small squares and mix with the minced meat
For six pounds of prepared meat, add five ounces salt, one dram of powdered pepper, one dram of broken peppercorns in grain, and three drams of saltpeter
Mix everything exactly and let rest overnight
Fill beef intestines or other large intestines, press the meat down firmly with a smooth stick, and tie like a bundle of tobacco
Leave in the curing room for eight days to cure well in salt mixed with equal quantity of saltpeter
Dry in the chimney or over smoke, coating with wine lees in which sage, thyme, bay leaf, and basil have been boiled
When dry, wrap in paper and store in ash

description: Prepared with meat, lard, and saltpeter.

ingredients.name: Lard, half a pound for each pound of meat
ingredients.sourceText: Lard, half a pound for each pound of meat

ingredients.name: Salt, one ounce per pound of meat
ingredients.sourceText: Salt, one ounce per pound of meat

steps: Mince the wild boar meat with half a pound of lard for each pound of meat
Season with one ounce of salt per pound of meat and spices in proportion
Add a little crushed saltpeter to make the meat red
Place the seasoned mixture in a bowl with a little muscatel wine
Marinate for twenty-four hours
Prepare intestines of the desired thickness and soak them to remove the tripe flavor in white wine with thyme, laurel, basil, garlic, shallots, and salt
After draining well, fill the intestines with the wild boar meat using a funnel
Tie the ends
Hang in the chimney to smoke until the sausages are completely dry
Cook over coals for one hour, although some people eat them raw

title: Salchichones Reales (Royal Sausages)
description: Prepared with partridge, hen, and capon.

ingredients.name: Fattened young hen meat, raw and minced
ingredients.sourceText: Fattened young hen meat, raw and minced

steps: Mince very finely the raw meats of partridge, fattened young hen, and capon, along with a little raw ham, beef leg, and lard
Add parsley, onions, mushrooms, and earth truffles to the minced mixture
Season with salt, pepper, fine spices, and a pinch of garlic
Add two egg whites and five or six egg yolks and a little cream
Chop everything finely and incorporate well together
Roll this mixture into large pieces according to the desired quantity
Flatten thin slices of beef pulp on the table and wrap each sausage piece in these slices, making each at least as thick as an arm and of proportionate size
Line a pot with slices of ham
Place the well-wrapped sausages in the pot
Cover with slices of beef and other strips of ham
Cook over low coals (brasa) for eight to ten hours
Allow them to cool in the same pot
Remove any fat and carefully remove the wrapping meat without breaking the sausages
Cut into slices and serve cold

description: Prepared with pork, beef, and bacon.

ingredients.name: half its weight in beef shreds
ingredients.sourceText: half its weight in beef shreds

ingredients.name: salt per every six pounds of prepared meat

steps: Choose lean short pork meat and add half its weight in beef shreds and half its weight in bacon, which will be cut into pieces while the other two are minced together
Season adding five ounces of salt for every six pounds of prepared meat, ground and broken pepper and three-eighths of niter, whose mixture will be blended as well as possible
The next morning fill the veal intestines or other widest veal intestines you can get, crushing the meat well with a wooden mallet
When well full tie them strongly
Put them in a cauldron, letting them bathe in salt mixed with an equal part of niter for eight days
After that remove to smoke and bathe with wine dregs in which sage, thyme, laurel and basil have been boiled
When dry wrap them in paper to preserve them in ash

description: Prepared with fat, mutton, and truffle.

ingredients.name: Mutton loin, equal amount to chicken meat
ingredients.sourceText: Mutton loin, equal amount to chicken meat

steps: Remove the skin from two fat chickens without tearing it, keeping it whole if possible
Mince the chicken meat with an equal amount of mutton loin, earth truffles, ham, and lard
Incorporate all the minced meat together
Add a little cream of milk, four raw egg yolks, fine herbs, spices, salt, and pepper to the mixture
If the chicken skin came off whole, fill it with the prepared mixture; if divided, wrap the mixture in the skin pieces
Tie it appropriately and cook over white coals (brasa blanca)
If serving as an entrance course, add a good bound essence to the cooking liquid
If serving as an intermediate course, season the coals more strongly and serve the mortadella cold at the table

title: Salmis o Salmorejo de Chochas (Woodcock Salmis)
description: Prepared with bread, bread crumbs, and white wine.

ingredients.name: half a quarter of white wine
ingredients.sourceText: half a quarter of white wine

ingredients.name: two good spoonfuls of Spanish sauce
ingredients.sourceText: two good spoonfuls of Spanish sauce

steps: Clean and empty three or four woodcocks and place them on the spit
Finely chop the intestines with salt and coarse pepper, and arrange this mixture on toasted bread slices
Place the toasted bread beneath the woodcocks while they are cooking so they receive the fat that drips from them
After cooking and once cooled, divide them by separating the wings, breast, and thighs, which are placed in a pot with bread crumbs

Mash the remaining parts well and form a paste with them, then place this paste in another reduced pot with half a quarter of white wine, coarse pepper, nutmeg, and two good spoonfuls of Spanish sauce
Let everything boil together and pass it through a strainer or fine sieve over the pieces that were left in the other pot with the bread crumbs
Heat everything without boiling, add lemon juice, and serve
When arranging on the plate, place the toasted bread slices that received the fat, cut in heart shape

title: Salmon à la Ginebrina (Genevan Salmon)
description: Prepared with salmon, red wine, and carrots.

ingredients.name: one salmon steak of two or three pounds
ingredients.sourceText: one salmon steak of two or three pounds

steps: Choose a good salmon steak of about two or three pounds, clean and scale it, and place in a saucepan.
Moisten with red wine and add two carrots, three sliced onions, two cloves, a bay leaf, salt, pepper, parsley sprigs, and some whole scallions.
Let the salmon cook for an hour and a half over low heat.
Ten minutes before serving, pass the cooking liquid through a sieve and pour into a saucepan with a good piece of butter kneaded with flour.
Place over heat and stir strongly until it boils, letting it reduce until only enough sauce remains to cover the salmon steak, skimming and degreasing as it reduces.
Drain the fish, place on a fish platter, and cover with the sauce after passing it through cheesecloth, finishing with two small pats of butter.

title: Salmuera (Brine)
description: Prepared with water and salt.
steps: Fill a bronze pot or other pot of appropriate size with water
Place it on the fire and when it boils, gradually add white salt, letting it dissolve

To determine the necessary quantity, first place an egg in the boiling water; when it rises to the surface and holds itself there by itself, it is a sign that the water is well salted and the brine is made
Remove from heat and let cool in the pot, or in a bronze or tin pot, and pour into earthenware vessels if it is a copper pot, because the verdigris that would form in it is very harmful
Only pour into the curing place when it is cold, as otherwise it would give an unpleasant taste to the meats to be cured
If the brine is not to be used immediately but saved for when needed, skim it, remove from heat, let it cool and settle, strain without disturbing the sediment, and store for use

title: Salmón Amoratado (Purple Salmon)
description: Prepared with salmon, wine, and carrots.
steps: Empty the salmon without cutting the belly

After washing and drying well, put it in a fish kettle with eight bottles of wine, seven or eight carrots, sliced onions, four cloves, six bay leaves, a little thyme, salt and a handful of parsley sprigs
The salmon must be bathed in its broth and left to cook over low heat for two hours
When ready to serve, drain it, place a napkin on the fish kettle with the salmon on top surrounded with parsley
If it is to be served as a main course, put a good piece of butter in a pot and mix three tablespoons of flour and one large tablespoon of brown fish or beef stock
Put the sauce on the fire, stirring until it boils, and at that moment add whole pepper and let it reduce

title: Salsa (Gran) o Aspic (Grand Sauce or Aspic)
description: A sauce made with beef, partridge, and hen.

ingredients.name: 2 eggs with whites, yolks and shells
ingredients.sourceText: 2 eggs with whites, yolks and shells

steps: Put beef knuckles, old partridge, hen, poultry feet and ham in a pot, tying them together
Add 2 carrots, 2 large onions and a well-seasoned bunch of herbs
Moisten with a little concentrated broth
Let sweat slightly over fire
When the sauce is becoming gelatin and turning yellow, moisten with broth or water and allow to reduce more than before
Skim when it reaches boil and add necessary salt
Let cook three consecutive hours
Degrease and strain through a wet, wrung-out cloth and let cool
Break 2 eggs with whites, yolks and shells, beat them
Moisten with a little of the small broth and add 1 tablespoon of tarragon vinegar with a good glass of white wine
Mix all this with the grand sauce, put it on the fire and stir with a boxwood brush
When it begins to boil, move it to the edge of the stove so it only simmers without boiling
Cover the pan and place fire on its lid
When the aspic is seen to be liquid, strain it through a wet, wrung-out cloth, tying it to the four feet of a frame or stool
Empty into the pan, cover it again with its lid, placing a little fire on top
Once the fire is finished, the grand sauce is complete and ready to use

title: Salsa Bechamela Magra (Lean Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cream, wheat flour, and shallots.

ingredients.name: A good amount of whole pepper
ingredients.sourceText: A good amount of whole pepper

ingredients.name: Mushrooms or mushroom trimmings if available
ingredients.sourceText: Mushrooms or mushroom trimmings if available

ingredients.name: A very small piece of sugar

ingredients.name: A little butter to mix in at serving time

ingredients.name: A little cream if needed to thin it out
ingredients.sourceText: A little cream if needed to thin it out

steps: Bring 12 quartillos of cream to a boil
Dissolve 4 tablespoons of common wheat flour into the cream
Place the pot over a high heat so the sauce does not take color, and stir constantly until it becomes thick enough for your intended use
Prepare separately: put 2 or 3 shallots, 1 carrot cut into strips, scraped nutmeg, a good amount of whole pepper, salt, a small mixed bunch of herbs, and mushrooms or their trimmings in another pot
Make this preparation boil with 2 glasses of water while the milk is reducing
When the milk has reduced to the proper point, incorporate the other preparation gradually and slowly, as adding it all at once would curdle it
Add a very small piece of sugar, because it is necessary that its taste not be perceived
Keep a little butter warm in a bain-marie to be mixed into the sauce at the time of serving
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little cream

title: Salsa Bretona (Breton Sauce)
description: A sauce made with onions, garlic, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: well-cooked white beans, mashed
ingredients.sourceText: 1 cup of well-cooked white beans, mashed

ingredients.name: A good piece of very fresh butter
ingredients.sourceText: A good piece of very fresh butter

steps: Remove the beards and tails from some large headed onions and slice them thin
Place them in a pot with a good piece of butter, salt, pepper, garlic, thyme, and laurel
Fry everything over moderately high heat until the onion has browned
Move the pot to a low fire, cover it, and place a little heat or embers on the lid
When the onion is cooked, put it back over a more intense fire and add a little sugar and vinegar
Let everything reduce until the onion begins to curdle
Add a little tomato sauce and 1 cup of well-cooked white beans that have been mashed
Pass everything through a strainer and let it simmer over low heat with a good piece of very fresh butter
This sauce is commonly served with beans or green beans

title: Salsa de Jitomate a la Italiana (Italian Tomato Sauce)
description: A sauce made with tomatoes, bay leaf, and broth.

ingredients.name: Equal quantities of jitomates (tomatoes) and onions
ingredients.sourceText: Equal quantities of jitomates (tomatoes) and onions

ingredients.name: One tablespoon or half, according to the quantity of jitomates, of saffron powder
ingredients.sourceText: One tablespoon or half, according to the quantity of jitomates, of saffron powder

ingredients.name: Broth with fat from the pot
ingredients.sourceText: Broth with fat from the pot

steps: Use equal quantity of jitomates and onions, and season them with one bay leaf, crushed pepper, and one tablespoon or half of saffron powder, according to the quantity of jitomates.
Moisten the jitomates and onions with broth from the pot that has fat, and add the necessary butter.
It should cook over low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon so that it does not stick.
Strain through a sieve using a wooden spoon for this purpose.

title: Salsa de Mantequilla (Butter Sauce)
description: A sauce made with butter, salt, and pepper.

ingredients.name: 1 piece of butter the size of a walnut
ingredients.sourceText: 1 piece of butter the size of a walnut

steps: Season with salt, pepper, 2 cloves and nutmeg, {{source-4}} dissolved in water and a piece of butter the size of a walnut
Allow the sauce to form over heat, stirring and keeping it more watery than thick
After boiling for a little more than a quarter hour, remove from heat and mix in 1 pound of butter, sliding it in little by little and stirring always so it does not turn into oil
Add a little vinegar and pass through cloth over a water bath

title: Salsa de Mostaza Indiana a la Francesa (Indian Mustard Sauce, French Style)
description: A sauce made with egg yolks, chiles, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: good oil, in quantity equal to the yolks
ingredients.sourceText: good oil, in quantity equal to the yolks

ingredients.name: small chiles, in quantity equal to the spoonfuls of oil
ingredients.sourceText: small chiles, in quantity equal to the spoonfuls of oil

steps: Grind a dozen hard egg yolks
Moisten them with good oil, adding it little by little in a quantity equal to that of the yolks, so that it mixes with them while continuously grinding
Add, without ceasing to grind, one spoonful of saffron, small chiles in quantity equal to the spoonfuls of oil, one glass of vinegar, coarse pepper, and salt
When everything is well ground, mashed, and mixed, pass this sauce through a cloth, which should have the appearance of a substance and be very thick

title: Salsa de Mostaza Verde (Green Mustard Sauce)
description: A sauce made with mustard, chervil, and chives.

ingredients.name: two to three raw egg yolks
ingredients.sourceText: two to three raw egg yolks

ingredients.name: four to five spoonfuls of vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: four to five spoonfuls of vinegar

steps: Gather a small handful of chervil, the same amount of pimpinella, tarragon, and small chives
Blanch all these herbs and, pressing them well, mash them
Add salt, coarse pepper, and one glass full of mustard, and grind everything together again
Add half a glass of oil that will be mixed exactly with the rest
When everything is well thinned, add two or three raw egg yolks and four or five spoonfuls of vinegar
Stir everything and pass through a cloth
If the green color is not pronounced enough, it can be enhanced with spinach green

title: Salsa de Ravigote (Ravigote Sauce)
description: A sauce made with capers, egg yolk, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Fine herbs: parsley, scallion, chervil, and celery
ingredients.sourceText: Fine herbs: parsley, scallion, chervil, and celery

ingredients.name: fat-free broth (for cooked version)
ingredients.sourceText: One cup of fat-free broth (for cooked version)

ingredients.name: Half tablespoon of flour (for cooked version)
ingredients.sourceText: Half tablespoon of flour (for cooked version)

steps: Grind the fine herbs - parsley, scallion, chervil, and celery - in a mortar with {{source-1}} and one or two anchovies if desired.
When everything is made into a paste, add one raw egg yolk, salt, pepper, {{source-6}}, and {{source-7}}.
Serve this sauce with cold meat.
If you wish to cook it, boil it for a quarter of an hour with one cup of fat-free broth.
When cooked, add fresh butter in proportion, kneaded with half a tablespoon of flour, and add salt, pepper, and more drops of vinegar.
Remove from heat as soon as the butter is melted and serve.

title: Salsa Española (Spanish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef, pheasant or partridges, and ham.

ingredients.name: ham (amount equal to half a beef strip)
ingredients.sourceText: ham (amount equal to half a beef strip)

steps: Put 2 beef strips, 1 pheasant or 4 partridges, ham equal to half a beef strip, 4 or 5 large carrots and 5 onions (one studded with 5 cloves) in a pan
Moisten the meats with 1 bottle of dry Madeira wine and 1 ladle of gelatin
Put the pan over high fire
When the broth has almost consumed, reduce to low fire
When the gelatin is a deep yellow, remove the pan from the fire and leave it for ten minutes so the gelatin can release well
Sweat the pieces of meat from the lower part of the beef strips, the same way as was done with these for the main sauce, and moisten that sauce with its broth
Well skimmed, dissolve a little red substance in it and pour it over the meat
Add mushrooms, a bunch of parsley and onion, some shallots, thyme and bay leaf
Once the sauce boils, place it in a corner of the stove so it only simmers gently until the meats are cooked
This sauce should have a beautiful color, neither too dark nor too light

title: Salsa Mahonesa (Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, vinegar, and lemon or vinegar.

ingredients.name: A few drops of lemon or vinegar
ingredients.sourceText: A few drops of lemon or vinegar

steps: Place two raw egg yolks and a few drops of vinegar in an earthenware dish
Mix well with a wooden ladle
Slowly add very fine oil in a continuous thin stream, almost drop by drop, stirring constantly
When the oil begins to bind with the yolks, add a few drops of lemon or vinegar without stopping stirring
Add oil and drops of acid alternately
If too thick when serving, soften with a little vinegar and season with salt and sometimes pepper
If the oil does not bind with the egg and they appear separated, place one or two yolks in another earthenware dish and slowly add what has broken, stirring constantly until it comes together

title: Salsa Morena (Brown Sauce)

Strain this substance and add the red substance that has been prepared separately
Let boil again for one hour
Degrease the sauce and strain through cheesecloth
